Named unit test passes, and the first call on a store blocked by a v4 connection rejects with UpgradeBlockedError (name and message per A-3; the blocker stays at v4). But spec section 7 maps the 'blocked then never unblocked' edge case to SPEC-02: every call rejects and each retry also gets blocked and rejects, with no hang. Observed: the second call on the same store while the blocker is still open stays pending (still pending after 10 s), and resolves only after the blocker closes. The same happens for readSettings() after the first rejection. A raw probe in real Chromium and WebKit shows the same platform rule: a second open request for the same database waits in the queue behind the still-pending blocked request and gets neither 'blocked' nor an error until the blocker closes.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected (spec section 7, SPEC-02): while another connection keeps blocking the upgrade, every store call rejects with UpgradeBlockedError and nothing hangs, including retries after the first rejection. Actual: the first call rejects, but the next call on the same store (count(), readSettings(), etc.) stays pending indefinitely while the blocker stays open (observed > 10 s), because its new open request waits behind the earlier blocked request, which is still pending. It settles only when the blocker closes. Real Chromium and WebKit queue a second open the same way, so in the app any store call after the first failure (for example opening Statistics or saving a hand) still hangs for as long as the blocking tab stays open.
findings.fix: While a blocked open request is still pending, new store calls must reject promptly with UpgradeBlockedError instead of starting another open that queues behind it. Once the blocker closes, the next call must succeed, as SPEC-03 already requires. Add a unit test for a second call made while the database is still blocked that expects a prompt UpgradeBlockedError rejection.

summary: 7 of 8 SPEC items pass; the Tab-order and layout work (SPEC-05..08) and the raw-record test (SPEC-01) are solid, and end to end passes on npm run dev in Chromium and WebKit. Integrity PASS. SPEC-02 FAIL (HIGH, J-1-01): the spec's never-unblocked edge case is not met. A retry while the blocker is still open hangs instead of rejecting, because the new open queues behind the earlier blocked request.
